raw_response:
I farm the way people around Quzhou County usually keep land productive and risk low, so this year I will stay with the wheat-maize rotation. That fits my place, my experience, and the weather pattern here in the North China Plain. If I already have winter wheat in the ground at the start of the season, I will push that crop through harvest with fertilizer, water, and pest control at the key stages, then I will turn the same land quickly into summer maize so I do not lose time or moisture. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it matters because I care most about stable yield, not experimenting. I will keep tillage simple, use fertilizer at moderate rates, irrigate when the crop most needs it, and spray only when pressure is real, because I want dependable production and manageable costs.
